draft.title: Hubble's law
card: Hubble's law says the recession speed of a distant galaxy is proportional to its distance from us: v = H₀d. Here v is the speed at which the galaxy moves away, d is its distance and H₀ is the Hubble constant.
A galaxy twice as far away recedes twice as fast. Galaxies in every direction show this pattern.
The speed comes from the red shift of the galaxy's light. The distance is found by other methods, such as using standard candles, which are objects of known luminosity.
H₀ is about 70 km/s per megaparsec. A galaxy 100 Mpc away would recede at about 7000 km/s. Hubble's law shows that space itself is expanding.
draft.remember: Recession speed is proportional to distance, so the universe is expanding.

a.q: Galaxy A is 200 Mpc from us. Galaxy B is 100 Mpc away. By Hubble's law, how do their recession speeds compare?
opts: A recedes twice as fast as B
A recedes at the same speed as B
A recedes half as fast as B
A recedes four times as fast as B
a.why: Speed is proportional to distance, so doubling the distance doubles the speed. Four times as fast would need distance to be squared, but the law is a direct proportion.
a.clue: v = H₀d is a direct proportion.

b.q: Using H₀ = 70 km/s per Mpc, a galaxy recedes from us at 14 000 km/s. About how far away is it?
b.why: Rearrange to d = v ÷ H₀ = 14 000 ÷ 70 = 200 Mpc. Multiplying speed by H₀ gives 980 000, which wrongly treats H₀ as a factor for distance rather than a divisor.
b.clue: Rearrange v = H₀d to make d the subject.

a.best: A recedes twice as fast as B

check.summary: No problems found. The facts check out (H₀ ≈ 70 km/s/Mpc, 100 Mpc gives about 7000 km/s), and both questions have a single correct answer that matches the explanations.
